title: Dialogue: meeting someone on a train
description: Follow and take part in a complete first conversation with a stranger, line by line.

guide.title: The situation
guide.text:
Tom, a visitor from England, gets on a train to Jaipur and finds a free seat next to Anita, who is travelling home. The phrases of this unit are the lines of their conversation in order. The note on each line says who is speaking.

Read the whole dialogue through first, then practise each line. Nearly everything in it comes from earlier units: greetings, 'where are you from', the continuous tense, the future, and the 'to me' pattern.

The two speakers use आप to each other throughout, as strangers do. Because Tom is a man and Anita a woman, the dialogue also shows you both sets of verb endings side by side.

examples.native: नमस्ते, क्या यह सीट खाली है?
examples.roman: namaste, kyaa yah seet khaalee hai?

guide.title: Who is speaking to whom
guide.text:
Watch the verb endings change with the person being described.

Tom asks Anita आप कहाँ जा रही हैं?, with रही, because आप here is a woman. Anita answers मैं जयपुर जा रही हूँ, with रही for herself. When Tom speaks about himself he says जा रहा हूँ and सीख रहा हूँ.

When Anita asks Tom where he will stay, she says आप कहाँ रुकेंगे?, with the masculine ending -गे. To a woman it would be रुकेंगी. Her offer चाय पिएँगे? ('will you drink tea?') is masculine for the same reason.

If you are a woman, practise Tom's lines with रही, and expect questions put to you to end in रुकेंगी and पिएँगी. If you are a man, practise Anita's lines with रहा.

guide.title: Phrases worth stealing
guide.text:
आपकी हिंदी बहुत अच्छी है! You will hear this compliment after your first three words of Hindi. Languages are feminine, so आपकी and अच्छी. A modest reply is मैं अभी सीख रहा हूँ, 'I am still learning'; अभी, 'right now', gives the sense of 'still'.

भारत आपको कैसा लग रहा है?, 'how is India seeming to you?', is the question every visitor is asked. Answer with बहुत अच्छा. Replace भारत with any place or thing: दिल्ली आपको कैसी लग रही है? (दिल्ली is feminine).

यहाँ के लोग, 'the people of here', shows that के can follow यहाँ and वहाँ: यहाँ का खाना, 'the food here'.

आपसे मिलकर अच्छा लगा, 'it felt good to meet you', is a slightly warmer alternative to आपसे मिलकर खुशी हुई.
